reason: The text explicitly demonstrates Yahweh's goal to help and liberate the Hebrew people. Key evidence includes: (1) Yahweh's direct command to Moses: 'Let my people go and serve me' (שַׁלַּח עַמִּי וְיַעַבְדֻנִי); (2) Divine protection of Hebrew dwellings in Goshen from the plague of swarms ('I will set apart the land of Goshen where my people stand so there will be no swarms'); (3) The Israelites receive light during the plague of darkness while Egyptians experience three days of complete darkness ('all the children of Israel had light in their dwellings'); (4) Yahweh's explicit purpose stated to Moses: 'Let you know that I am Yahweh' through these signs, establishing His power to save Israel. The entire narrative demonstrates a clear pattern of Yahweh distinguishing between the Egyptians (who suffer the plagues) and the Hebrew people (who are protected or spared), working systematically to achieve their liberation from Egyptian bondage.
